cards.explanation: The answer is the Philistines. David defeats them, subdues them, and takes Gath and its villages from their hand. The chapter opens with a win and doesn't slow down. I'm still catching my breath, and I only read it.

The answer is that they serve David and bring tribute. The Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute. The text says they became subject to him, so this wasn't a fifty-fifty deal. Subject means under him, and tribute is what they brought.

The answer is False. David captures a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers and twenty thousand foot soldiers. But he hamstrings all the horses except a hundred that he keeps for the chariots. The text tells us what he does and doesn't give a reason, so I'll leave it there.

The answer is troops to hold the land. David places garrisons in Aram of Damascus. A garrison is a group of soldiers stationed in a place. After that, the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute.

The answer is the LORD! The chapter says it plainly: "So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went." Look at all the battles packed in here, and the writer still stops to say who is behind them. I like a chapter that gives credit where it's due.

The answer is Solomon, David's son. The passage says David took a large amount of bronze from Tibhath and Cun, and with it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and various bronze articles. David gathers the metal, and a son uses it. Solomon becomes king after David (1 Chronicles 29:28), and that's some serious handing down.

The answer is True. Tou, king of Hamath, sends his son Hadoram to bless David for defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. So David's win was good news in Hamath. I think Tou was glad somebody finally dealt with Hadadezer, but that part is only my guess.

The answer is that David dedicates it to the LORD. King David dedicated all of it to the LORD, the gifts from Hadoram and the silver and gold from all those nations. Piles of treasure, and he gives it to the LORD. I think I'd be tempted to stare at that pile awhile, so I'm impressed.

The answer is False. The text says that all the Edomites were subject to David. Abishai, son of Zeruiah, placed garrisons in Edom after the battle in the Valley of Salt. The chapter then says again that the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.

The answer is True! The text says, "Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people…" The chapter moves from battles to how David ruled. After all that fighting, it's good to see the kingdom run with justice and righteousness.
